title: Outlook for Mac: conversational email drafting, editing and formatting with Copilot (Worldwide)

claims.where: controls[0].note; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Disabling content-analysis connected experiences removes Copilot features across Excel, OneNote, Outlook, PowerPoint and Word, rather than only this feature.
claims.quote: If you turn off connected experiences that analyze your content on devices in your organization, Microsoft Copilot features won't be available to your users in the following apps: Excel; OneNote; Outlook; PowerPoint; Word

claims.claim: The documented content-analysis restriction applies to current versions of the listed apps on Windows, Mac, iOS and Android.
claims.quote: This applies to when you're running the most current version of these apps on Windows, Mac, iOS, or Android devices.

claims.claim: The Mac preference and Cloud Policy provide equivalent content-analysis controls, and the Mac privacy page permits either approach.
claims.quote: You can also use Cloud Policy and these five policy settings: ... Allow the use of connected experiences in Office that analyze content

claims.claim: Mac privacy preferences can be enforced through a configuration profile or MDM server.
claims.quote: These new preference settings are CFPreferences API compatible and can be set using the defaults command in Terminal, or enforced through a Configuration Profile or Mobile Device Management (MDM) server.

claims.claim: Subscribed users signed in with a work or school account cannot themselves turn off content-analysis connected experiences.
claims.quote: If the user has a Microsoft 365 (or Office 365) subscription and is signed in with a work or school account ... then the user can't turn off connected experiences that analyze content.
